paper_metadata.title: Zero-Shot Text-to-Image Generation
paper_metadata.abstract: Text-to-image generation has traditionally focused on finding better modeling assumptions for training on a fixed dataset. These assumptions might involve complex architectures, auxiliary losses, or side information such as object part labels or segmentation masks supplied during training. We describe a simple approach for this task based on a transformer that autoregressively models the text and image tokens as a single stream of data. With sufficient data and scale, our approach is competitive with previous domain-specific models when evaluated in a zero-shot fashion.

extraction_data.innovation: Autoregressive transformer that models text and image tokens as a single stream of data; uses a discrete VAE (dVAE) with an 8192-vocabulary codebook to compress images into tokens, eliminating the need for complex architectures, auxiliary losses, or side information (e.g., segmentation masks) during training.
extraction_data.pretraining_task: Autoregressive modeling of the joint distribution over text and image tokens
extraction_data.pretraining_corpus: 250 million text-image pairs from the internet (JFT-300M scale), including Conceptual Captions and a filtered subset of YFCC100M
extraction_data.application: Text-to-image generation, image editing, zero-shot visual synthesis
extraction_data.tokenizer: BPE for text, discrete VAE (dVAE) with 8192 vocabulary for images
extraction_data.attention_mechanism: Sparse decoder-only self-attention with causal, row, column, and convolutional masks, Standard multi-head self-attention (Transformer), Sparse attention (row, column, convolutional masks), Multi-head self-attention (qkv matrices)
extraction_data.training_pipeline: Two-stage: (1) Train discrete VAE encoder/decoder on images; (2) Concatenate up to 256 BPE-encoded text tokens with 1024 image tokens and train autoregressive transformer to model joint distribution
extraction_data.quantization_precision: 16-bit mixed precision (1-6-9 format for running mean, 0-6-10 for running variance), 16-bit, 16-bit floating point, 16-bit (bfloat16/float16), 1-6-9 format for gradients
extraction_data.optimizer_innovation: Adaptation of PowerSGD for billion-parameter scale with custom 1-6-9 format and grouped all-reduce to fix performance regressions
extraction_data.benchmark_result: MS-COCO zero-shot generation preferred over prior work by human evaluators 90% of the time; FID: best by ~6 points with slight blur; IS: highest with blur radius >= 2; Human evaluation: chosen as most realistic 90.0% of time, best matching caption 93.3% of time
extraction_data.weight_clipping_mechanism: Gradient clipping by norm (threshold 4) during warm-up; per-resblock gradient scaling
